steps.title: The Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how have things been since your filler with us? I usually hear one of three things. Still happy with how it looks, it's starting to soften, or it's pretty much gone. Which one is closest for you?

(Only three answers. Tap the one you hear.)

steps.title: Still Happy With It
steps.content:
That's great to hear, {{contact_first_name}}. That's exactly what we hope for when someone finishes treatment with us. {{provider_name}} will be glad to know you're still happy with the results.

(Let them respond, then continue.)

steps.title: Starting to Soften
steps.content:
That happens, {{contact_first_name}}. Filler softens over time, and the face keeps changing on its own. It's not anything you did wrong. Your notes say you were happy with how it turned out. What kept you from coming back in?

(Let them answer. Stay warm. Do not book yet.)

steps.title: Pretty Much Gone
steps.content:
I'm sorry to hear that, {{contact_first_name}}. Filler does soften and wear off over time. It's not anything you did wrong. Your notes say you were happy with the result. Was it cost, timing, or something else that kept you from coming back?

(Let them answer. Stay warm. Do not book yet.)

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
While I have you, {{contact_first_name}}, can I ask you a few quick questions about anything else you've noticed?

(Wait for the yes. It's their file, so almost everyone says yes.)

steps.title: The Transition: Ask Permission
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, you said the result has softened. We'll come back to that. First, can I ask you a few quick questions so your file is up to date?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down every area they name. You'll recap them in a moment.)

{{contact_first_name}}, I'm going to run through a few changes people often notice. Just let me know which ones apply to you, even if they're subtle.

First, your lips. Have they thinned out again, or are they still where you want them?

How about your cheeks, any volume loss making them look flatter than they used to?

What about the smile lines, the ones that run from your nose to the corners of your mouth?

Any hollows under your eyes that make you look tired when you're not?

How about your jawline and chin, anything there you'd like more defined?

Any little lines around your mouth, the kind lipstick settles into?

How about the lines on your forehead or between your brows?

And the skin itself, has it been looking rough or dull lately?

Any sun spots or uneven tone showing up?

Last one. Any loosening or sagging, especially along the jaw or neck?

(Recap what you wrote down, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, of those, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(They already named one area. Write down every area they name, including that one.)

{{contact_first_name}}, I'm going to run through a few changes people often notice. Just let me know which ones apply to you, even if they're subtle.

First, your lips. Have they thinned out again, or are they still where you want them?

How about your cheeks, any volume loss making them look flatter than they used to?

What about the smile lines, the ones that run from your nose to the corners of your mouth?

Any hollows under your eyes that make you look tired when you're not?

How about your jawline and chin, anything there you'd like more defined?

Any little lines around your mouth, the kind lipstick settles into?

How about the lines on your forehead or between your brows?

And the skin itself, has it been looking rough or dull lately?

Any sun spots or uneven tone showing up?

Last one. Any loosening or sagging, especially along the jaw or neck?

(Recap everything, including what they mentioned at the start, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, between what you mentioned earlier and these, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'd like to ask a few quick questions about {{main_concern}} so your file is up to date. It'll only take a minute.

(Ask these three questions in order. Pause after each and let them answer.)

How long has it been bothering you, like a few weeks, or more like months?

(Let them answer. If it fits, you can say "Got it.")

Is it something you notice now and then, or every time you look in the mirror?

(Let them answer. If it fits, you can say "I see." or "I understand.")

When it's at its worst, does it ever interfere with photos, going out, or feeling put together?

(Let them answer. If they name an impact, reflect only what they said; if they mention photos, you might say "You notice it in photos." If none, you can say "Got it, thank you.")

steps.title: The Review
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, let me make sure I have this right.

(Read back their three answers: how long, how often, what it gets in the way of.)

So it's been on your mind a while, and you notice it most times you look in the mirror. At its worst it gets in the way of what you mentioned. Did I get that right?

(Say what they named: photos, going out, or feeling put together. Let them answer. If they correct you, take the correction and move on.)

And it sounds like you'd really like to look in the mirror and feel good about it again. Is that fair to say?

(Most people say yes. Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: The Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that's worth getting looked at instead of just dealing with it. Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in so {{provider_name}} can take a look at {{main_concern}}. If we can help, we'll walk you through the options. If it's not the right fit, we'll say so. Either way you'll know where you stand. Does that sound reasonable?

(Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: They Hesitate: Find Out Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, you said {{main_concern}} is something you'd like to feel better about. I don't want to assume anything. Is it the timing, or is something else holding you back?

(Stay easy about it. No pressure. Do not repeat the concern back at them. Let them answer.)

steps.title: Uncover the Real Concern
steps.content:
Okay, {{contact_first_name}}. I'm not going to push you on it. What's the part giving you pause?

(Let them answer. Then tap what you hear.)

steps.title: Nothing Found: Why Did They Stop?
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm glad you're still happy with it.

Can I ask what changed that led you to stop coming in?

(Let them answer. Listen all the way through. Do not argue with it.)

Filler softens slowly, so most people don't notice it going until it's gone. A check-in now and then keeps the look you like. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in for a check-in so you keep the look you have. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Objection: “It wore off, so what’s the point?”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Filler is meant to soften over time, so that's not a sign it didn't work.

Can I ask, did it fade evenly, or did one area go first?

(Let them answer.)

The face keeps changing on its own, and filler settles into it as it goes. What lasted, how long, and where it went first all tell us something. That's useful information about {{main_concern}} now, and it's information we didn't have the first time.

{{provider_name}} can look at where things sit today and tell you what would hold. Sometimes that's a small touch-up. Sometimes it's a different approach than last time.

Would it help to know which one before you decide anything?

steps.title: Objection: “I didn’t see enough of a difference”
steps.content:
I appreciate you telling me, {{contact_first_name}}. That's worth hearing.

Can I ask, was it that you couldn't see it, or that nobody else noticed?

(Let them answer. Do not promise results on the call.)

Those are two different things. A subtle result is often what people ask for, and then it feels like nothing happened. Other times the amount or the placement wasn't the right call for {{main_concern}}. Your notes show exactly what was done, so we're not guessing.

{{provider_name}} can look at {{main_concern}} today and hear what you were hoping for. Then you'll hear plainly what would get you closer.

Is that worth one visit to find out?

steps.title: Objection: “I’m nervous about looking overdone”
steps.content:
That's a good worry to say out loud, {{contact_first_name}}. Most people share it.

Can I ask, is that from something you've seen on others, or how you felt after your own visit?

(Let them answer. Do not promise a look on the call.)

What you're describing usually comes from too much, too fast, in the wrong spot. That's the opposite of how we'd approach {{main_concern}}. You've been here before, so {{provider_name}} already knows how your face responds. The goal is that people say you look rested, not that you look different.

The visit is where you get to say exactly that, out loud, before anything is decided.

Would it help to come in and set that line in person?

steps.title: Objection: “I went somewhere else”
steps.content:
That's okay, {{contact_first_name}}. I'm glad you kept it up.

Can I ask, are you still going there, or has that lapsed too?

(Let them answer. Stay easy. Do not ask why they left.)

Either way, your whole history is here, including what was used, how much, and where. That matters with filler, because what’s already in the face changes what makes sense next. Starting from a full record is safer than starting from memory.

{{provider_name}} can take a look at {{main_concern}} and pick up where things left off, with nothing repeated by accident.

Would you be open to coming back in for that?

steps.title: If They Say: “I was happy with my results”
steps.content:
That makes sense, {{contact_first_name}}, and that's the best reason there is. When you like what you see, coming back stops feeling urgent. The thing with filler is that it softens so slowly you don't notice it going. Does that make sense?

(Let them answer.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you back on the schedule so you keep the look you like. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: Cost or Budget
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}, and I'm glad you told me. A check-in is just a look. You're not committing to anything. It's one visit so we can see how everything is holding.

Does that seem fair?

(Let them answer.)

(Do not quote prices, packages, or discounts. The office handles that.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you back on the schedule. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: “Life got busy”
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Life fills up fast, and this kind of thing gets pushed down the list. It happens to everyone. A check-in visit is quick, and we can find a time that works around your schedule.

Would that work?

(Let them answer.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you back on the schedule at a time that's easy for you. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: “I’ll come back when it wears off”
steps.content:
That's a fair way to think about it, {{contact_first_name}}. The one thing I'd share is that filler goes slowly. By the time you notice it's gone, it's been going for a while. It's easier to keep the look you have than to start over.

Does that sound right?

(Let them answer.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you back on the schedule before it's gone. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: They Moved or Tried Another Provider
steps.content:
That's understandable, {{contact_first_name}}. Things change. If you're still in the area, we'd love to see you again. Your whole history is in your file, so we can pick up right where you left off.

Would that be okay?

(Let them answer.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you back on the schedule. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Objection: “I’m considering another option”
steps.content:
That's fair. Can I ask what you're looking at, like a different treatment, another injector, or just leaving it?

(Let them answer. Do not knock the other option.)

Those can all make sense, and some people do well combining them. The part that's hard to compare from home is what would move {{main_concern}} for you. {{provider_name}} already knows how your face responded last time, so you're not starting over here.

Come in, get a straight answer on where things stand, and then compare. If the other option turns out to be the better fit, you'll be choosing it for a reason.

Is that a fair way to decide?

steps.title: Objection: Cost
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}. Is it the cost of the visit itself, or the thought of the full amount again?

(Let them answer. Do not quote prices, packages, or discounts. The office handles that.)

This first visit is one appointment, not a package. You'll hear what anything past that costs before you decide on it. And since you've been here before, we're not starting from scratch, and starting from scratch is the expensive part.

The other side of it is what {{main_concern}} is already costing you, the things you mentioned a minute ago. That's the part I'd hate to see keep adding up.

Can we at least get the look on the calendar?

steps.title: Objection: “I don’t have time”
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Is it finding time for the first visit, or the worry about coming back every few months?

(Let them answer.)

Right now we're only talking about one visit. {{provider_name}} looks at {{main_concern}} and tells you what it would take from there. Sometimes that’s a small touch-up. Sometimes it’s a different plan than last time, and you’ll hear that up front so you can decide. Nobody is booking you into a schedule on the phone.

We'll fit that first visit around your schedule, not the other way around.

Could you find a short window for that?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to talk to my spouse”
steps.content:
Of course. Is it more about the money side, or do you two just make these decisions together?

(Let them answer. If it's money, use the cost answer.)

That's fair, and I'm not asking you to commit to anything they'd need to weigh in on. Right now, all you can tell them is that {{main_concern}} is on your mind. After the visit, you can tell them what's going on and what it would take. That's an easier conversation to have. And if they'd like to come along, they're welcome.

Can we pencil it in, and you can move it after you two talk?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to think about it”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Usually when someone says that, there's one specific thing on their mind. What's the part you'd want to think over?

(Let them answer. If they name cost, time, or another reason, tap that button.)

Okay. I'm not trying to rush you. The one thing I'd say is that {{main_concern}} is on your mind. It's been that way for a while, and it hasn't sorted itself out on its own. The visit is how you get the information you'd be thinking with. You can think it over just as easily after you know what's going on.

Would it be easier to think it over once you have the answers?

steps.title: Objection: “Just send me some info”
steps.content:
I can do that, {{contact_first_name}}. What would you want it to cover, so I send the right thing?

(Let them answer. If they name cost, time, or another reason, tap that button.)

I'll be straight with you, though. Anything I send is going to be general. It can't tell you what's realistic for {{main_concern}} specifically. That takes {{provider_name}} looking at your face, and that's one short visit.

Let's do both. I'll send the information, and we'll put a time on the calendar. If what I send answers your question, you can call and cancel, no problem.

Does doing both work for you?
